messages:
Dev Patel: heads up — SRE is planning a controlled regional failover test (low-risk slice) and we need to align support macros + escalation handling. goal is “degraded but available” during the window, but some customers may notice latency blips / brief reconnects.

Link to comms template (internal): https://confluence.redwoodinference.com/display/ONCALL/Controlled+failover+test+-+customer+comms+template

Can someone from SRE confirm: expected customer-visible symptoms, what we should/shouldn’t promise, and when Support should page vs just log a SUP ticket?

Owen Phillips: +1. also can we get a single macro we can paste for: (a) hosted API users, (b) dedicated customers w/ pinned region, (c) “what’s happening?” responses when they see 5xx. Right now we’re ad-libbing and it’s inconsistent.

Tomáš Novák: jumping in. for the controlled test window we want Support to use a consistent “planned reliability exercise” message, and we should avoid saying “zero impact.”

Customer-visible symptoms we saw in staging:
- transient `5xx` bursts (typically <60s) on a subset of requests during cutover
- elevated tail latency (p95/p99) while routing converges
- streaming: occasional disconnects requiring client retry
- some customers may see routing headers change regions (if they inspect)

Hard “should NOT happen” (page immediately): sustained elevated error rate >5min for non-test traffic, or evidence we’re failing over the wrong tiers.

Aisha Bello: adding SLO framing — we’re treating this as a controlled mitigation test, but customers may see brief degradation. please don’t commit to specific p95 numbers in support replies.

Suggested Support guidance:
- acknowledge
- recommend retry w/ exponential backoff
- if they’re streaming: confirm client handles reconnect/resume
- if they’re Dedicated and pinned: tell them we’ll keep within their policy; if they opted out of cross-region routing they may see errors rather than failover

Rafael Mendes: escalation path proposal (for the test window):
1) If customer reports issues: open SUP + include tags `controlled-failover-test` and `region:<us-east|us-west|eu-west>` and `product:<hosted|dedicated|private>`
2) Page SRE only if ANY of:
   - customer is enterprise + impact > 3 minutes OR repeated failures after retries
   - you see multiple inbound tickets with same symptom/region within 10 minutes
   - customer provides evidence of sustained 5xx/timeout beyond 5 minutes

Otherwise route to #incidents only (no page) with the SUP link so we keep a single thread.

Connor O'Brien: release/change mgmt note: we’ll post a heads-up in #announcements + #incidents 30 min before the start, and again when it’s complete. Support should not proactively reach out to customers unless they ask / they’re already escalated.

Support Bot: Reminder: when filing SUP tickets, include request IDs + approximate timestamps + customer org ID. Use /support-escalate to tag the oncall.

Owen Phillips: can we get actual macro text (short + long)? also status page guidance — are we posting “maintenance” or keeping it internal unless something goes sideways?

Tomáš Novák: status page: for the controlled test, default is *no* status page post unless we hit stop conditions or there’s customer-visible impact beyond the test cohort. if we do post, use “Investigating / Monitoring” language, not “maintenance,” since it’s an availability event.

Macro draft (short):
“Thanks for reporting this. We’re running a controlled reliability test to validate automated regional failover. During the window you may see brief elevated latency or intermittent errors. Please retry your request (exponential backoff). If the issue persists for more than a few minutes, reply here with request IDs and we’ll escalate.”

Macro draft (streaming add-on):
“If you’re using streaming responses, you may see a disconnect during routing convergence. Reconnect and retry; ensure your client handles resume/retry on network interruption.”

Dev Patel: this is good. request: add one line for Dedicated customers about traffic isolation + what “failover eligible” means without exposing internal details.

Rafael Mendes: dedicated-safe wording:
“For Dedicated deployments, behavior depends on your configured routing/failover policy. If cross-region failover is enabled for your capacity, traffic may be temporarily served from a secondary region to reduce errors. If it’s disabled, you may see intermittent errors until the primary region stabilizes.”

Aisha Bello: +1. also please don’t tell customers “we failed you over” unless we confirm via SRE; say “traffic may be routed” / “we may route.”

Owen Phillips: can we lock these into a single internal macro doc and link from the comms template? also what’s the best place to drop SUP links during the window—#incidents or here?

Connor O'Brien: SUP links go in #incidents during the window so IC + observers see it in real time. keep #support for macro/triage chatter. :thumbsup:

Dev Patel: 👍 I’ll update our internal macro page w/ the text above and add: tags + paging thresholds + request-id checklist. We’ll also pin the Confluence comms template link in #support for the week of the test.
